title: Air-fryer salmon teriyaki
subtitle: Salmon fillets glazed with a simple teriyaki sauce and air-fried until caramelised.
excerpt: Salmon fillets marinated in soy sauce, mirin, and honey, then air-fried until the glaze caramelises and the fish is just cooked through. Ready in 15 minutes. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking method in which fish or meat is glazed with a mixture of soy sauce, mirin, and sugar and grilled or pan-fried. Teriyaki salmon became one of the most widely made Japanese-influenced dishes in British home cooking from the 2000s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 1 hour in the fridge.

content.text: The teriyaki glaze caramelises quickly at high heat, which is why salmon teriyaki needs attention in the last 2 minutes of cooking. The sugar in the mirin and honey chars at the edges of the fillet ,  this is correct and adds flavour, but watch for the difference between charring and burning. A 20-minute marinade is enough; longer makes the fish slightly salty throughout.

Mix {{soy-sauce-light}} of light soy sauce, {{mirin}} of mirin, and {{honey}} of honey in a shallow dish. Add the {{salmon-fillet}} fillets skin-side up and spoon the marinade over the flesh. Leave for 20 minutes.

Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Line the basket with a small square of baking paper or spray with oil. Place the fillets skin-side down. Spoon any remaining marinade over the top. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the glaze is caramelised and the flesh is opaque when pressed at the thickest part. Drizzle with sesame oil if using, before serving.

items.cause: Temperature too high or cooked too long.
items.fix: Check at 8 minutes. The caramelised edges should be dark but not charred black throughout. If burning, reduce the temperature to 180°C for the final 2 minutes.

items.symptom: Glaze not sticking to the fillet
items.cause: Fillet not dried before marinating, or marinade too thin.
items.fix: Pat the flesh side dry before adding to the marinade. If the soy sauce is thin, reduce the marinade in a small pan for 2 minutes before using.

items.cause: No lining or oil in the basket.
items.fix: The teriyaki glaze caramelises and sticks. Line with baking paper or spray the basket before cooking.

content.text: Air-fryer salmon teriyaki is a quick weeknight dinner. Serve over steamed rice with a few sliced spring onions and a drizzle of sesame oil, or alongside stir-fried greens. The same marinade and method work for cod loin, chicken thigh, or firm tofu.
